```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
set.seed(1)
```

## 1. What is different from SAEforest

`SAEforestLearner` is a fork of `SAEforest` 1.0.1 (Krennmair & Frink). The estimator of domain means is the
mixed effects random forest (MERF) of Krennmair & Schmid (2022), with the same nonparametric bootstrap for the
MSE; the original functions (`SAEforest_model()`, `MERFranger()`, `summarize_indicators()`, the generics) keep
their names and arguments. The differences are in how the computation is organised and in what the fixed part
of the model can be.

| | SAEforest 1.0.1 | SAEforestLearner |
|---|---|---|
| Population | a `data.frame` in memory | a `data.frame`, or a raster streamed from an on-disk cache (`SAEpopulation()`), tens of millions of units |
| Memory of the bootstrap | grows with population × `B` (dense matrices) | only domain sums are kept; bootstrap errors are drawn in C++ per replicate |
| Forest prediction | `ranger::predict` (sorts every covariate at each call) | flattened forests predicted in C++ (`flatten_forest()`), bit-identical |
| Output | domain means | means and totals (`total_factor`), with exact bootstrap MSEs of any aggregation (`SAEaggregate()`) |
| Transformation | none | optional Box-Cox MERF with empirical-best-type back-transformation (`transform = "boxcox"`) |
| Fixed part of the model | a `ranger` forest | **any supervised learner** (`learner = `): ranger (default), xgboost, lightgbm, glmnet, mgcv, lm, or user-defined (`sae_learner()`) |
| Out-of-sample predictions of the sample units | out-of-bag predictions of the forest | out-of-bag when the learner has them, otherwise K-fold cross-fitting (`oof_folds`) |
| Convergence of the MERF iterations | relative change of the log-likelihood | the same (`em_criterion = "original"`, default with ranger) or a robust criterion for stochastic learners (`"robust"`: windows, patience, best iteration kept) |
| Tuning | `tune_parameters()` (ranger, random CV) | `tune_learner()` + `spatial_folds()`: spatial-block CV of the mixed model for any learner |
| Reproducibility | `set.seed()` | `seed` argument; identical results for any number of cores |

With `learner_ranger()` (the default) the point estimates are identical to those of the original package.
The bootstrap random streams differ from version 2.0.0 of this package by two draws (see `NEWS`), so MSE
estimates with a given seed are equal in distribution but not bit by bit.

The scalable engine is used whenever domain means (or totals) are requested from unit-level population data
(`meanOnly = TRUE`, the default). Nonlinear indicators and aggregated covariate data still run the original
code (`engine = "legacy"`), with the forest only.

## 2. The learner interface

A learner is an object of class `sae_learner` with two mandatory functions,

* `fit(x, y, args, threads)`: fits the learner to the covariates `x` (a data.frame, one row per sample
  unit) and the working target `y`; `args` is the list of learner parameters, `threads` the number of threads;
* `predict(model, x, threads)`: returns one prediction per row of `x` (a data.frame, or a numeric matrix
  for the population);

and optional ones: `oof(model, x, y, args, threads)` (out-of-sample predictions of the training units that
the fit provides for free, e.g. out-of-bag predictions), `pack(model)` / `unpack(packed)` (a compact,
serialisable form of the model for the bootstrap workers and the disk), `info(model)` (what `summary()`
shows), plus `packages` (loaded in the workers), `args` (default parameters) and `bounded` (whether the
predictions are bounded by the range of the training target, as for tree ensembles).

Two rules make a learner work in the parallel bootstrap: the functions must be **self-contained** (they are
sent to the workers without their enclosing environment: call package functions as `pkg::fun` and keep the
parameters in `args`), and the `...` of `SAEforest_model()` are passed to `fit()` through `args`, so ranger
parameters such as `num.trees` must not be passed with other learners.

The MERF algorithm itself does not change: it alternates the learner, fitted to the target minus the current
random effects, and a linear mixed model of the random intercepts with the learner's out-of-sample predictions
as offset. When the learner has no out-of-sample predictions, they are obtained by K-fold cross-fitting at
every iteration (and in the bias correction of the error variance), so that the random effects and the
bootstrap residuals are never based on over-fitted in-sample predictions. With a linear learner
(`learner_lm()`, exact leave-one-out predictions) the iterations converge to the nested-error linear mixed
model, i.e. the EBLUP of the domain means.

## 3. Use case: the eusilc example data with three learners

The example data of `SAEforest` (synthetic EU-SILC data for Austria: 1,945 sample and 25,000 population
units in 94 districts) are used with small settings (`B = 10`, 100 trees, 2 cores) so that the vignette runs
in a few minutes. The target is equivalised income; the numeric covariates are used.

```{r data}
library(SAEforestLearner)
data("eusilcA_pop")
data("eusilcA_smp")
smp <- eusilcA_smp
X <- smp[, -c(1, 2, 16, 17, 18)]   # numeric covariates (gender dropped)
names(X)
```

### 3.1 The default learner: ranger

```{r ranger}
t0 <- Sys.time()
m_rf <- SAEforest_model(Y = smp$eqIncome, X = X, dName = "district", smp_data = smp, pop_data = eusilcA_pop,
                        MSE = "nonparametric", B = 10, B_adj = 10, num.trees = 100, total_factor = 1,
                        seed = 1, cores = 2, verbose = FALSE)
t_rf <- difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs")
m_rf$PopInfo$learner
head(summarize_indicators(m_rf, MSE = TRUE, CV = TRUE)$ind, 4)
```

### 3.2 A predefined learner: gradient boosting (xgboost)

The parameters of the learner are given to its constructor; `oof_folds` sets the cross-fitting (5 by
default); the robust convergence criterion is used automatically.

```{r xgboost, eval = requireNamespace("xgboost", quietly = TRUE)}
t0 <- Sys.time()
m_xgb <- SAEforest_model(Y = smp$eqIncome, X = X, dName = "district", smp_data = smp, pop_data = eusilcA_pop,
                         MSE = "nonparametric", B = 10, B_adj = 10, total_factor = 1, seed = 1, cores = 2,
                         verbose = FALSE, learner = learner_xgboost(nrounds = 150, eta = 0.05, max_depth = 4),
                         oof_folds = 5)
t_xgb <- difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs")
m_xgb$PopInfo$learner
c(iterations = m_xgb$MERFmodel$IterationsUsed, best = m_xgb$MERFmodel$BestIteration)
```

### 3.3 A user-defined learner: support vector regression (e1071)

A learner is defined with `sae_learner()`. The functions below are self-contained: `e1071::svm` is called
with its namespace, the kernel parameters travel in `args`, and `predict` works both on the sample
data.frame and on the population matrices. A radial kernel with scaling is used; `pack` keeps the model as
is (an `svm` object is serialisable).

```{r svm, eval = requireNamespace("e1071", quietly = TRUE)}
learner_svm <- function(cost = 1, gamma = NULL, epsilon = 0.1) {
  sae_learner(
    name = "svm",
    packages = "e1071",
    args = list(cost = cost, gamma = gamma, epsilon = epsilon),
    fit = function(x, y, args, threads) {
      m <- if (is.matrix(x)) x else data.matrix(x)
      args$importance <- NULL                      # a ranger argument added by the engine: ignore it
      if (is.null(args$gamma)) args$gamma <- 1 / ncol(m)
      e1071::svm(x = m, y = y, type = "eps-regression", kernel = "radial", scale = TRUE,
                 cost = args$cost, gamma = args$gamma, epsilon = args$epsilon)
    },
    predict = function(model, x, threads) {
      m <- if (is.matrix(x)) x else data.matrix(x)
      as.numeric(stats::predict(model, m))
    },
    info = function(model) list(type = "support vector regression (radial)", support_vectors = model$tot.nSV)
  )
}
t0 <- Sys.time()
m_svm <- SAEforest_model(Y = smp$eqIncome, X = X, dName = "district", smp_data = smp, pop_data = eusilcA_pop,
                         MSE = "nonparametric", B = 10, B_adj = 10, total_factor = 1, seed = 1, cores = 2,
                         verbose = FALSE, learner = learner_svm(cost = 2), oof_folds = 5)
t_svm <- difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs")
summary(m_svm)
```

### 3.4 Comparing the three models

The point estimates of the district means are close for the three learners, while the variance
components and the MSEs differ with the learner. The comparison is on the model side only: which learner
is *right* for a given application is a question for cross-validation on held-out units (`tune_learner()`,
next section) and for simulation.

```{r compare, eval = exists("m_xgb") && exists("m_svm")}
cmp <- data.frame(district = m_rf$Indicators$district, ranger = m_rf$Indicators$Mean,
                  xgboost = m_xgb$Indicators$Mean, svm = m_svm$Indicators$Mean)
round(cor(cmp[, -1]), 3)
rmse_pct <- function(m) 100 * sqrt(m$MSE_Estimates$Mean) / m$Indicators$Mean
data.frame(learner = c("ranger", "xgboost", "svm"),
           sigma_u = round(c(m_rf$MERFmodel$RanEffSD, m_xgb$MERFmodel$RanEffSD, m_svm$MERFmodel$RanEffSD)),
           sigma_e = round(c(m_rf$MERFmodel$ErrorSD, m_xgb$MERFmodel$ErrorSD, m_svm$MERFmodel$ErrorSD)),
           median_RMSE_pct = round(c(median(rmse_pct(m_rf)), median(rmse_pct(m_xgb)), median(rmse_pct(m_svm))), 1),
           seconds = round(as.numeric(c(t_rf, t_xgb, t_svm))))
pairs(cmp[, -1], main = "District means by learner")
```

Totals and aggregates work the same way for every learner: `SAEaggregate()` uses the stored bootstrap
replicates.

```{r aggregate, eval = exists("m_svm")}
SAEaggregate(m_svm, unique(eusilcA_pop[, c("district", "state")]), name = "state")[, 1:6]
```

## 4. Choosing and tuning a learner with spatial cross-validation

`tune_learner()` fits the mixed model with the learner for every row of a parameter grid and every fold, and
summarises the accuracy of the held-out units (on the original scale when a Box-Cox transformation is
used). Folds should respect the spatial structure of the sample: `spatial_folds()` builds them from square
blocks. The example data have no coordinates, so random ones are drawn here only to show the mechanics.

```{r tune, eval = requireNamespace("xgboost", quietly = TRUE)}
coords <- cbind(runif(nrow(smp), 0, 100), runif(nrow(smp), 0, 100))
folds <- spatial_folds(coords[, 1], coords[, 2], block_size = 10, k = 4, seed = 2)
table(folds)
tn <- tune_learner(Y = smp$eqIncome, X = X, dName = "district", smp_data = smp, learner_fun = learner_xgboost,
                   grid = expand.grid(nrounds = c(100, 200), max_depth = c(3, 5)), folds = folds,
                   cores = 2, seed = 3, oof_folds = 3, eta = 0.05)
tn$results[, c("nrounds", "max_depth", "RMSE", "RMSE_se", "bias", "slope")]
tn$best[, c("nrounds", "max_depth")]
```

The same function with `learner_fun = learner_ranger` and a grid over `mtry` and `min.node.size` tunes the
forest, and with `transform = "boxcox"` and `bc_lambda` the comparison is made on the original scale of a
transformed model.

## 5. Box-Cox transformation with any learner

The transformation is independent of the learner: the model is fitted to `((y + shift)^lambda - 1) / lambda`,
and the domain means are the expected back-transformed values given the predicted random effects
(Gauss–Hermite quadrature on the transformed scale). Learners whose predictions are not bounded by the
training range (`bounded = FALSE`, e.g. linear models) get wider back-transformation tables automatically.

```{r boxcox}
smp$ypos <- smp$eqIncome - min(smp$eqIncome) + 1e5    # a positive target for the example
m_bc <- SAEforest_model(Y = smp$ypos, X = X, dName = "district", smp_data = smp, pop_data = eusilcA_pop,
                        MSE = "none", seed = 1, cores = 2, verbose = FALSE, learner = learner_lm(),
                        transform = "boxcox", bc_lambda = 0.5, bc_shift = 1)
head(m_bc$Indicators, 3)
```
